name: brk
description: brk() and sbrk() change the location of the program break, which defines the end of the process's data segment. brk() sets the end to a specified address, allocating or deallocating memory if possible. sbrk() increments the data space by a given amount, which can be used to allocate memory or query the current break.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: The desired new end of the data segment for brk()

parameters.name: increment
parameters.description: The number of bytes to increment the data space by for sbrk()

return_value.success: brk() returns 0; sbrk() returns the previous program break
return_value.failure: Returns -1 or (void*)-1 on error, and sets errno to ENOMEM

errors.description: The process would exceed its maximum data size or there is not enough memory

bugs: The glibc wrapper for brk() behaves differently from the kernel system call; various systems use different types for sbrk()'s argument. It is recommended to use malloc(3) instead for portability.
